jobs.description:
Sinch Telco is a standalone business within Sinch. Our products support communications services for mobile operators around the globe. Our systems are backend systems that communicate with other backend systems. You will not find them on Sinch's public website. We are protocol heavy and regard USSD, SMPP, Diameter, and SIP as about as much frontend it gets in our domain. We are looking for an experienced software engineer with focus on AI-driven Development, to further accelerate adoption of AI-powered development practices across Sinch Telco.

In this role, you’ll be a hands-on practitioner, leveraging AI agents to design, build, verify and deliver our type of software while shaping how AI is applied in our software development. Together we move toward a paradigm where software developers manage teams of specialized AI agents for requirements analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and deployment. We intend to unlock new capabilities that enable teams to build and ship faster with higher quality, security, and maintainability.

You have a vision for the future of AI-driven software development but understand that progress requires practical steps and patience. You demonstrate value through hands-on work and tangible results. You collaborate well with experienced colleagues as a peer and respect existing domain knowledge while contributing new perspectives and influence through the quality of your work. You are self-directed, proactive, and comfortable operating with ambiguity. The AI tooling landscape changes rapidly and you are energized by this pace.
As our Software Engineer, you will:
Work in a team as a highly productive, hands-on software engineer, leveraging agents to deliver features and products across multiple areas.
Lead by example to spread best practices, workflows, and tooling for AI-assisted development for coding, testing, documentation, and deployment.
Assist in evaluation, selection, and configuration of AI development tools and agent frameworks to improve software development.
Define clear requirements and product direction with a product management perspective in cooperation with product managers and team members. 

REQUIREMENTS
Extensive software engineering experience, with a proven ability to design, evaluate, and evolve software architectures.
Solid understanding of complex distributed backend systems. Experience with telecom systems, BSS/OSS, or messaging infrastructure is a plus.
Hands-on experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools such as Copilot, Cursor, Claude, for production software delivery, not just experimentation.
Experience working with AI-driven development workflows, including autonomous coding agents and multistep task orchestration.
Ability to define clear, structured, and decomposable requirements for both engineers and AI agents, with strong product awareness and long-term stability.
Practical experience with Model Context Protocol. Experience with multi-agent frameworks is a plus.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts, document approaches, and collaborate effectively across teams.

Our corporate language is English, please submit your application in English.
We are not supporting relocation at this time. Applicants must either hold a Swedish or EU/EEA citizenship or have a valid Swedish work permit.
OUR HIRING PROCESS 
We are committed to ensuring a recruitment process that is fair, objective, consistent, and inclusive.
We believe in a two-way process and encourage you to ask questions throughout the journey. If this role isn't what you're looking for, please explore the other opportunities listed on our career page: https://www.sinch.com/careers/. No matter who you are, we hope you find an exciting path forward - hopefully with us!

About us:
With more than 54 locations throughout Europe, the Bertrandt Group has been providing engineering and development solutions for the international automotive and aerospace industries since 1974. More than 12,000 employees use their know-how and innovative strength every day to support our customers – leading manufacturers and OEMs – with integrated solutions in management, design, and industrialization.
Bertrandt is now expanding into Sweden, establishing a strong and future-oriented presence in Gothenburg. Our activities cover a spectrum of expertise from electrical, electronics, and software development to design engineering, project management, quality, industrialization, and validation, all driven by innovation and a passion for technology.

The research group in Electronic Systems at the Department of Computer Science, Electrical and Space Engineering at Luleå University of Technology is established in the areas of electronic design, electrical measurement technology, electromagnetic compatibility, and modelling and measurement of power grids and energy systems. We are active in education as well as in externally funded research projects carried out in collaboration with industry, municipalities and grid operators. We have access to a number of laboratories and to a test bed in an inland municipality in northern Sweden, with a physics-based model of the local distribution grid and measurement nodes in the grid. To strengthen our research in digital twins for power grids, buildings and EV charging, we are now looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow with ambitions within academia. 
 
 
Subject description 
 
Electronics systems include electronics design, measurement technology and electromagnetic compatibility for control, monitoring and instrumentation of technical processes and systems, with close connection to applications and applied research. 
 
 
Project description 
 
The electrification of vehicles, heating and services means that local power grids and buildings need to interact in new ways. Power is often lacking in the grid during the hours when demand is highest, although the grid is lightly loaded for much of the year. Using the existing capacity safely requires better knowledge of the state of the grid, but in smaller distribution grids measurements are often sparse and delayed.
 
Digital twins, where physics-based models are combined with measurement data and forecasts, are a promising way to address this. Important research questions are how such models can be kept up to date with few measurement points, how uncertainty in model and data can be quantified and propagated to decisions, and how the model results can be turned into signals that buildings, EV charging and other flexible loads can follow, while maintaining comfort, function and electrical safety.
 
A digital twin is never better than the measurements it is built on. This is where the group's competence in electronics and measurement technology contributes. We develop our own measurement nodes that are placed in the grid, with sensors, embedded systems and local data processing, and we study how measurements from new nodes and from existing smart meters can be combined. Questions such as where measurements are most useful, what accuracy and time resolution are needed, and how the system handles data loss and delays are part of the research. 
 
You will work in a research project in this area, in collaboration with a municipality and a local grid operator. The project builds on an existing physics-based grid model and measurement nodes already installed in the grid, and the methods are tested both in real municipal buildings and on open benchmark networks, so that the results are useful for other municipalities and grid operators. 
 
 
Duties 
 
The work will mainly include research connected to the project described above. This includes modelling of distribution grids and of the power demand of buildings, state estimation and uncertainty analysis with sparse measurements, analysis of which measurements and measurement nodes are most useful, contribution to the further development of the measurement nodes, simulation and evaluation of control of flexible loads, and analysis of real measurement data. The results are published in scientific journals and conferences. The work is carried out in close collaboration with the project partners and includes recurring travel to the test bed. Supervision of students and active participation in our fundraising activities will be included in the tasks with a maximum of 20% of working hours. 
 
 
Qualifications 
 
To qualify for this position, you must have a Ph.D., a doctoral degree or a foreign degree corresponding to a Ph.D. or doctoral degree in electrical engineering, electric power engineering, control engineering, energy engineering or related subjects. Persons who have completed a doctoral degree no more than three years before the end of the application period are prioritized. You must have very good skills in the English language, both orally and in writing.
 
Experience of power flow analysis and modelling of distribution grids (for example pandapower, PowerFactory or similar) is an advantage. Experience of digital twins or combinations of physics-based and data-driven models, state estimation, uncertainty analysis or probabilistic methods, control of flexible loads, building energy systems or EV charging infrastructure, measurement systems, sensors and embedded systems, as well as programming in Python and work with real measurement data, is also an advantage. Knowledge of Swedish is an advantage, since the work is carried out in close dialogue with a municipality and a grid operator. 
 
 
Further information 
 
Full-time fixed term employment for two years, with the possibility of a third-year extension. Placement in Luleå, with recurring travel to the test bed. Starting: by agreement.
 
The employment is subject to the project being granted funding. 
 
 
We strive for a gender balance on the project and particularly welcome applications from women.
